advocate.case:
DRIVEN, not undriven: the proposal was spiked in a scratch clone of eeffe347, passed the full gate there (GATE: PASS, tests passed=4968 failed=0) and was run through every next step listed in `driven`.

THE ROBUST POSITION. The fork was raised on one door (`jigc setup`) and one looping route. Driven past that door, on the candidate (dded1fac…) and identically on the previous release (accf3996…, so regression: false throughout), the layouts whose home is no work tree are not "partial" — jigc lands exactly ONE doc there and then stops. Four constructions driven: a worktree beside a bare repository, a worktree behind a bare `.git`, a `--separate-git-dir` checkout, a submodule.
- `jigc setup`: exit 1 after writing (beside-bare, separate-git-dir), re-run as routed exit 1 with the same refusal; exit 0 in a submodule and behind a bare `.git`, with the install written into `<super>/.git/modules/vendor/` plus the SUPERPROJECT's pre-commit hook rewritten, or into the folder holding the bare `.git`.
- First doc finalizes at exit 0. Then `jigc doc list` prints "no committed docs"; `jigc validate` exits 1 with six blocking findings in three layouts (five are `schema-conformance.home-vacated` for CHANGELOG.md, VISION.md etc. that never existed).
- The SECOND doc's `jigc task finalize` exits 3 in all four: `reconciliation.rename — tracked managed doc adr:cache … is missing`, while the file is on disk and in HEAD. Its route's arms do not lead out: "restore" a file that is there, or `jigc unmanage`, which exits 1 with a bare git error (beside-bare, separate-git-dir) or exits 0 by un-managing a healthy committed doc (submodule).
- `jigc milestone create` exits 1 in all four. `jigc uninstall` exits 1 in all four with a route whose precondition already holds; `jigc uninstall --force` exits 1 in two of them after removing `.jigc/`, its route loops, and `.claude/` is left in a folder that is no repository.
- A LOSS AT EXIT 0 (the first clause's subject, not the second's): an untracked file of the user's at a doc's home (`docs/decisions/cache.md`) is replaced by `jigc task finalize` at exit 0 in all four layouts, on both binaries; afterwards no file under the root and no git object holds its bytes (before-control found the marker; every blob of `git cat-file --batch-all-objects` searched). The same walk in a plain checkout refuses at exit 3 and keeps the file. Cause: `cli::task::git_home_claims` asks nothing where the home is no checkout — its own doc comment says so.
One cause for all of it, in one function: `cli::repo::jigc_home` returns `dirname(git-common-dir)` whether or not a checkout stands there.

THE TELLS.
1. Hollow declared surface: clause 2 is "a working product others can use and rely on"; a reader in a submodule gets exit 0 and "adapter installed" at setup and cannot land a second doc. Four doors' printed routes (setup, task finalize, uninstall, uninstall --force) lead back into themselves or at a command that fails — the letter of "every refusal's route works as printed", which carries no regression term.
2. One-way door. decisions-pending.md's (D) row owes "whether these three layouts are supported — and if they are not, a refusal that says so at setup, rather than doors that half-work". Leaving it as it is is NEITHER of the two answers the record names; it is the half-working doors the row says are not to stand. And each answer is cheapest now: after 1.0.0 a refusal at setup breaks two exit-0 success paths of the release (submodule, behind a bare `.git`) under the regression rule "what succeeds on the previous release's binary in a layout must succeed on the candidate"; and the supported answer becomes a store-location migration on a released major, where today the only installs at the old home are ones that wedged after one doc.
3. Committed trajectory: the human's ruling on the regression set (DECISIONS.md 2026-10-06, part 2) lists "a worktree of a bare repository · a separate git directory · a submodule" among "the nine ordinary configurations and layouts"; that instrument is owed before the first run can close and its fixtures for three of nine states cannot honestly be built on a setup that exits 1 and a store one doc deep. design/storage.md defines jigc_home as "the main checkout" — the noun is the design, `dirname(git-common-dir)` an implementation of it that is false in exactly these layouts. design/assistant-adapter.md holds the hook install to "resolve the real hooks dir".
Where the record leans the other way, honestly: clause 1's scope sentence names four ordinary configurations and these are not among them; the declared-bounds row lists "the layouts whose home is no work tree" among bounds still to be written; (D)'s trigger is M57. The record does not settle it — what is new is what was driven after it was written.

THE STOCK RATIONALIZATIONS, REFUTED. "Pre-existing / no regression" is not "not needed": the route measure has no regression term and the loss is clause 1's; and the deferral rests on a record first written from a reading, then corrected to "rc.24 creates and finalizes a doc" — true, and one doc deep. "Any fix takes the decision" is why this is a halt, not why it waits; and it is not premature generality — no new stored file, registry, flag or finding code: the predicate "is this directory a checkout of this repository, asked of git" was built by the fix pass for these same layouts (`home_is_a_checkout`), and the proposal asks it where the home is resolved instead of at two guards afterwards. "Not provable yet": proved on synthetic layouts on every door named.

THE PRICED COST OF THE CHEAP CUT. A 1.0.0 that destroys an untracked file at exit 0 in layouts the regression ruling calls ordinary — or a declared bound whose written reach must read "anyone in a submodule, a worktree of a bare repository or a separate git directory; setup reports success in two of four constructions; the second doc cannot be landed; a file at a doc's home is replaced". Every round re-finds it (three reporters of this round's one door, a triage row, a verifier, this case), because the review rows run every printed route. M57 inherits both answers at their dear price, and the special cases written around the wrong home (`InstallSubject::NoWorkTree`, the skip in `git_home_claims`, the silence in `CodeOnlyCheckout::differing`) stay in the tree. Saved now: one fix cycle on one function, and one ruling.

THE ROBUST SCOPE (minimal-correct, not most thorough). One rule in `cli::repo::jigc_home`: a home is a checkout, or it is not the home. (1) `.git` a directory: unchanged. (2) `.git` a file and `dirname(git-common-dir)` is a checkout of this repository (asked of git): that directory — every ordinary linked and fan-out worktree, unchanged. (3) otherwise, the standing checkout is jigc's own fan-out worktree (`<home>/.jigc/worktrees/<id>`, `<home>` confirmed by the same question): `<home>` — a sibling cell found only by driving; without it `milestone finalize` exits 3. (4) otherwise: the standing checkout. Product half: one file, about 85 added lines; 36 call sites in 9 files reach the home through this one resolver. With it, all four layouts walk the whole lifecycle at exit 0, 76 of 78 step outputs byte-identical to the candidate's in a plain checkout (the two that differ are the setup ack's line naming where the hook went), and an ordinary linked worktree is unchanged (84 outputs compared, 0 differ). It treats the layouts as SUPPORTED — the decision (D) reserves for the human — and flips one standing parity pin.
What it does not do, each driven or stated: it does not migrate or remove an install an earlier build wrote at the old home (first command says "isn't set up — run jigc setup", that route works, committed docs are listed; the old directory and jigc's block in a superproject's hook stay — a MIGRATING note, not a mechanism); a linked worktree the user adds to a separate-git-dir or submodule repository is a home of its own; `jigc setup` typed in the folder holding a bare `.git` still installs there at exit 0 (unchanged, left open); cross-submodule management stays parked; it costs one more git command per home resolution in a linked worktree (`jigc start` 14 → 19, `jigc start --task` in a fan-out worktree 8 → 13).
The other answer, for comparison, NOT spiked: a refusal at setup needs a new finding code, turns two exit-0 success paths of the previous release into refusals, and closes one door only.

Caution: canary-one is a synthetic canary that closes nothing; the fork was argued as in a run that does. One sentence of the report under-claims: it says the previous release's `doc list` cell behind a bare `.git` was not driven; it was driven after the report was written and answers the same ("no committed docs").

VERDICT: robust-now — the cheap cut ships neither answer the record names, leaves an exit-0 loss and a one-doc wedge in layouts the regression ruling calls ordinary, and the minimal-correct fix is one resolver, gated green, with no new mechanism.

left_open: PD-1 (about the proposal, the reason holds is false): the pre-commit hook the proposal installs is inert in a worktree beside a bare repository, behind a bare `.git`, in a `--separate-git-dir` checkout and in the gitdir-pointer layout — a hand `git mv` of a managed doc commits at exit 0 where a plain checkout and the submodule block it. The proposal's tests only assert the hook is a file, so the gate is green over it. A variant of mine that clears GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_PREFIX from the probe's environment makes the hook block again in bare, behind and sep (driven on that step only).

The worktrees of one bare repository become separate homes that share one hooks directory: `jigc uninstall` in one removes the hook the others were installed with and tells nobody; the setup ack calls that hook 'local to this checkout'; a task open in one worktree is not listed in another.

For a submodule git can name the first checkout (core.worktree, asked at the git dir), so making the user's linked worktree of a submodule a home of its own — its own task list, no finalize.linked-worktree-doc guard — is a choice the human should see as one, not the absence of a source.

Source comments the proposal leaves stating the old rule: the doc comment of `home_is_a_checkout` in crates/cli/src/repo.rs and `InstallSubject::NoWorkTree` in crates/cli/src/setup.rs; (C) lists design docs and guides only.

An adopter's open task under the old home is unreachable after the change (task list empty, the staged ADR's authored slots left under the old .jigc/tasks/); the proposal names it and proposes a note only.

On the candidate and the previous release alike (not this proposal): one doc deep in all four layouts — second finalize exit 3, doc list empty, validate exit 1, milestone create and uninstall refuse, and an untracked file at a doc's home destroyed at exit 0 by task finalize. Reproduced; they stand whatever is ruled.
`jigc setup` typed in the folder holding a bare `.git` installs there at exit 0 on the candidate and on the proposal alike; the proposal does not close it and says so.

`jigc unmanage docs/decisions/cache.md` behind a bare `.git` on the candidate exits 0 claiming no file was at a path where one is — the advocate typed it on the previous release only; it is the same on the candidate.
The advocate's count '36 call sites in 9 files' was not reproducible: a search for `jigc_home(` under crates/cli/src finds 17 lines in 5 files. Not a step; nothing rests on it.

unverified.why: its verifier halted (The finding (item 6 of the staged-doc-ids report's Left open: Linux, and a root caller, were not driven) can only be verified by driving Repro V-2 on Linux and as uid 0. Neither was available: the handed candidate and previous release are both macOS arm64 images, the BINARY line names no trial image (so there is no Linux binary whose hash could be asserted, and a verifier builds none), and root is not reachable without a password. The block runs on macOS as written and was re-driven, but that is not the question the finding asks, and no reconstruction on macOS reaches Linux. A finding that could not be driven is not refuted; nothing red was observed, so it is not confirmed.)
